subject: TTFT + streaming cadence: follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: dylan_brooks, dev_patel
Date: 2026-11-08T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: TTFT + streaming cadence (recap & clarifications)

Thanks for the call today 





really appreciate the detailed walkthrough of RapidHealth's real-time note-taking use case. Below is a short recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can scope a focused POC.

Recap (from notes):
- Primary requirement: real-time transcription + model-generated summaries displayed live in clinician UI.
- Key perf targets you mentioned: TTFT (time-to-first-token) target <= 150 ms for streaming start, p95 <= 200 ms for subsequent tokens when under normal load.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~600 req/s; peak concurrency ~120 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: browser + mobile app clients. Prefer WebSocket for mobile; SSE is fine on modern web but some Android WebViews in your fleet have poor SSE support.
- Chunk cadence goal: client wants sub-100 ms chunk cadence for a smooth typing-like experience; typical chunk size 10-20 tokens.

Clarifying questions:
1) Can you confirm p95 TTFT (150 ms) is the hard requirement, or is p99 also relevant for SLA conversations?
2) What % of requests will be long-running streams (>30s) vs short (<5s)? Ballpark split helps sizing/eviction strategy.
3) Any hard constraints around encryption/KMS for the POC? You mentioned enterprise key management earlier.
4) Are you comfortable with a dedicated capacity POC (reserved nodes) or do you want to test on hosted first?

Next steps we recommend:
- Redwood will run a focused perf run against a representative model (+1 smaller/quantized variant) with your target payloads and streaming cadence.
- We'll share a TTFT runbook + SLO matrix and a short test harness you can run from your environment.
- Proposed timeline: perf run this week, 2-week POC starting next week if results are good.

Attachments: redwood-ttft-runbook.pdf, slo-matrix.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT + streaming cadence (recap & clarifications)

Thanks Marissa 




that's a solid summary. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: p95 <= 200 ms is the current internal bar; 150 ms would be ideal for the clinician UX. p99 matters for alerts, but our contractual SLA target will be p95.
- Stream lengths: roughly 70% of streams are short (3-8s), ~25% are medium (8-45s), and ~5% are long (45s+).
- Mobile support: we need WebSocket on iOS and Android native apps. Our mobile product team prefers WebSocket for stateful reconnection handling. Web UI can use SSE if that's simpler.
- Security: we require customer-managed KMS for key rotation during the POC; can provide details if needed.

We're open to a dedicated capacity POC if you think it will better represent steady-state economics. We'd like to pair the perf run results with an estimated cost-per-1M tokens for the config you benchmark.

Samir
Head of Product
RapidHealth
samir@rapidhealth.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-10T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT + streaming cadence (recap & clarifications)

Thanks Samir 


A few engineering notes and a proposed benchmarking plan: 

Notes:
- WebSocket vs SSE: WebSocket gives better tail behavior for mobile reconnects. We'll ensure the POC exposes both endpoints if you want to test both client stacks.
- TTFT drivers: cold model load, KV cache misses, and kernel launch overhead are the big factors. For TTFT <=150 ms we typically recommend warm workers, small batch windows, and an optimized token emission path (fast kernel + minimized serialization).

Benchmark plan:
1) Baseline: single-node perf with your representative payloads (short/medium/long) to capture TTFT p50/p95/p99 and chunk cadence.
2) Scaling: ramp to target concurrency (120) across a small cluster (3-5 nodes) to observe queueing and batching effects.
3) Streaming cadence check: emit at target token sizes (10-20 tokens) and measure inter-chunk intervals under load.

We can run baseline on Redwood hosted infra using a 4xA100 equivalent and also run a dedicated capacity configuration for apples-to-apples. We'll include a cost estimate per 1M tokens for each config.

Questions for you:
- Can you share a representative test audio -> prompt payload size (tokens) or transcripts so we can model decoding time?
- Do you have a preferred model? If not, we'll test one of our verified open models and a lower-precision quantized variant to show tradeoffs.

I can own the perf run with Dev on ops if you send the sample payloads.

- Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
